rationale:
Split into two children. Only one of them is a new DAG node; the other reuses an already accepted declaration.

**Why split.** Two steps of the supplied proof are self-contained and use none of this node's dependencies (bf_cone_density, bf_trichotomy, density_comparison).
- (i) Step 1, the inner compact (σ-compact) approximation of E.
- (ii) Step 3(c), Eilenberg's fibre-counting estimate: if E is Borel with Hᵏ(E) < ∞ and f is Lipschitz, the set of y whose fibre E ∩ f⁻¹(y) is infinite is Lᵏ-null.

(ii) is a classical, reusable theorem (Simon Ch. 2, 1.8(ii); Federer 2.10.25; HJJL Lemma 2.3). It is also the largest independent formal task in this proof: dyadic partitions, counting functions, measurable hulls and Fatou. The publication rules allow one tracked theorem per PR and no untracked named helpers. Without a split, all of (ii) would have to be inlined as local `have`s inside the parent theorem.

**Reuse.** Step (i) is exactly the comparator-accepted declaration `Submission.lpf_lli_inner_compact_approx`.
- Its node is root.lipschitz_pushforward_im-a1.locally_lipschitz_image-a1.inner_compact_approx-a1, status accepted, candidate d24e9e7b.
- The child copies its frozen Lean type, title and statement byte-for-byte; its proof is the accepted one, copied verbatim after a one-line provenance note.
- The controller therefore maps it to the existing node and creates nothing new: `_solve_children` resolves the name through `existing_by_name`, and `_workspace_payload` skips reused accepted theorems.

**Node budget.** max_nodes is 200 and dag.json holds 197 nodes. This split needs exactly one new node, `rectifiability_bf_infinite_fibre_null`. That name collides with nothing in dag.json or any decomposition file.

**What stays in the parent.** A new child may depend only on its own siblings, so every step that uses the parent's dependencies stays here:
- the countable a.e. bookkeeping over δ_l = 1/(l+1), via ae_all_iff and Measure.restrict_apply' with E′ Borel;
- the bf_cone_density sets;
- density_comparison with t = ⊤ and V = univ;
- the finite-fibre contradiction for points of E₃;
- the final union bound.

Two short glue facts also stay: L_v is Lipschitz, and Lipschitz images of Hᵏ-null sets are Lᵏ-null. All of these are short Mathlib/SimonGMT glue. Splitting them out would spend scarce node slots for no gain in safety.

**How the children give the parent.**
- Step 1: apply inner_compact_approx with P := N, μ := μHE[m+1], A := E. NullMeasurableSet comes from MeasurableSet, and SigmaFinite from IsFiniteMeasure, since μHE(E) < ∞. Taking E′ := ⋃ C_k gives a σ-compact Borel set E′ ⊆ E with μHE(E∖E′) = 0.
- Step 3(c): apply infinite_fibre_null with E := E′, f := L_v and K := ‖L_v‖₊. This gives Lᵏ(Y₃) = 0.
- All other steps of the supplied proof are unchanged.

**Verification.** I built frozen commit d8d46c9 in a scratch copy with the pinned packages (`lake build GMT.Ch06.Submission`). I then generated challenge files in the comparator's exact child scope, using `gmt-compare.py` `child_modules` in contract mode.
- The parent type, the reused type and the new type all elaborate, with only the expected `sorry` warning.
- In the same scope Lean checks two pieces of parent glue: the σ-compact Borel core E′ obtained from the reused type, and ∃ K, LipschitzWith K L_v (via LinearMap.toContinuousLinearMap).
- Every library name cited in the new child's proof was confirmed with `#check`.

These checks certify the statements and the glue. They do not certify the new child's proof.

**Caveat.** The controller's publication-recovery path (`parallel.child_publication_checkpoint`) accepts a reused child only once its status is `proved`. The normal path accepts `accepted`. This matters only if publication of this split ever has to be recovered.

subproblems.title: Compact inner approximation of σ-finite null-measurable sets in ℝ^P (parent step 3)
subproblems.statement: For every P ∈ ℕ, every measure μ on the Borel σ-algebra of ℝ^P, and every μ-null-measurable set A ⊆ ℝ^P such that the restriction μ⌞A is σ-finite, there are compact sets C_k ⊆ A (k ∈ ℕ) with μ(A ∖ ⋃_k C_k) = 0.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Eucl P)) (A : Set (Eucl P)), NullMeasurableSet A μ → SigmaFinite (μ.restrict A) → ∃ C : ℕ → Set (Eucl P), (∀ k, IsCompact (C k)) ∧ (∀ k, C k ⊆ A) ∧ μ (A \ ⋃ k, C k) = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Provenance: this is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.lpf_lli_inner_compact_approx (DAG node root.lipschitz_pushforward_im-a1.locally_lipschitz_image-a1.inner_compact_approx-a1, candidate commit d24e9e7b54d326f9d566fb5543e6cdea196355d1). It is reused here with its identical frozen Lean type, title and statement, and the proof below is its accepted parent-supplied proof, copied verbatim. In the selected parent it is applied in step 1 with P := N, μ := μHE[m+1] and A := E. NullMeasurableSet E holds because E is Borel. SigmaFinite(μHE⌞E) holds because μHE(E) < ∞ makes μHE⌞E a finite measure. Then E′ := ⋃_k C_k is σ-compact and Borel, E′ ⊆ E, and μHE(E ∖ E′) = 0.

Conventions. ℝ^P = Eucl P carries its Borel σ-algebra, μ is any measure on it, and μ⌞A = `μ.restrict A`. For a Borel set B, μ⌞B(E) = μ(E ∩ B) for every E ⊆ ℝ^P (Mathlib `Measure.restrict_apply'`); for a Borel set E, μ⌞A(E) = μ(E ∩ A) for every A (`Measure.restrict_apply`). 'μ-null-measurable' means measurable for the completion of μ (`NullMeasurableSet A μ`).

1. (Borel kernel.) Since A is μ-null-measurable, there is a Borel set A′ ⊆ A with A′ = A μ-almost everywhere (Mathlib `NullMeasurableSet.exists_measurable_subset_ae_eq`). In particular μ(A ∖ A′) = 0.

2. (Finite pieces.) Since μ⌞A is σ-finite, there are Borel sets S_m (m ∈ ℕ) with ⋃_m S_m = ℝ^P and μ⌞A(S_m) < ∞ for every m (Mathlib `spanningSets (μ.restrict A)` with `measurableSet_spanningSets`, `measure_spanningSets_lt_top`, `iUnion_spanningSets`). Put B_m := A′ ∩ S_m; it is a Borel set. Since B_m ⊆ A′ ⊆ A, we have B_m ∩ A = B_m, hence μ(B_m) = μ(B_m ∩ A) = μ⌞A(B_m) ≤ μ⌞A(S_m) < ∞.

3. (Inner regularity on one finite piece.) Fix m and put ν_m := μ⌞B_m, so ν_m(E) = μ(E ∩ B_m) for every E. Then ν_m(ℝ^P) = μ(B_m) < ∞, so ν_m is a finite Borel measure on ℝ^P. Since ℝ^P is a σ-compact metric space, every locally finite (in particular every finite) Borel measure on ℝ^P is regular (Mathlib `Measure.Regular.of_sigmaCompactSpace_of_isLocallyFiniteMeasure`; classically Simon Ch. 1, Theorem 1.15(2) with Remarks 1.16 and 1.12, or Ulam's tightness theorem for finite Borel measures on Polish spaces). In particular ν_m is inner regular with respect to compact sets on Borel sets of finite measure (Mathlib: `Regular` gives `InnerRegularCompactLTTop`, and then `MeasurableSet.exists_isCompact_sdiff_lt`, whose remaining hypotheses hold because ℝ^P is Hausdorff and its Borel σ-algebra contains the open sets). Applying this to the Borel set B_m, which has ν_m(B_m) = μ(B_m) < ∞, gives for every j ∈ ℕ a compact set K_{m,j} ⊆ B_m with ν_m(B_m ∖ K_{m,j}) < 1/(j+1). As B_m ∖ K_{m,j} ⊆ B_m, ν_m(B_m ∖ K_{m,j}) = μ((B_m ∖ K_{m,j}) ∩ B_m) = μ(B_m ∖ K_{m,j}). Hence μ(B_m ∖ K_{m,j}) < 1/(j+1) for all m, j ∈ ℕ.

4. (Null remainder in each piece.) Fix m. For every j, B_m ∖ ⋃_{j′} K_{m,j′} ⊆ B_m ∖ K_{m,j}, so by monotonicity and step 3, μ(B_m ∖ ⋃_{j′} K_{m,j′}) < 1/(j+1). Letting j → ∞ gives μ(B_m ∖ ⋃_{j′} K_{m,j′}) = 0.

5. (Global remainder.) Let x ∈ A ∖ ⋃_{m,j} K_{m,j}. If x ∉ A′, then x ∈ A ∖ A′. If x ∈ A′, choose m with x ∈ S_m (the S_m cover ℝ^P); then x ∈ B_m and x ∉ ⋃_j K_{m,j}, so x ∈ B_m ∖ ⋃_j K_{m,j}. Hence A ∖ ⋃_{m,j} K_{m,j} ⊆ (A ∖ A′) ∪ ⋃_m (B_m ∖ ⋃_j K_{m,j}). By monotonicity and countable subadditivity, together with steps 1 and 4, μ(A ∖ ⋃_{m,j} K_{m,j}) = 0.

6. (Re-indexing.) Let k ↦ (a(k), b(k)) := Nat.unpair k, a surjection ℕ → ℕ × ℕ because Nat.unpair (Nat.pair m j) = (m, j). Put C_k := K_{a(k), b(k)}. Each C_k is compact, and C_k ⊆ B_{a(k)} ⊆ A′ ⊆ A. By surjectivity, ⋃_k C_k = ⋃_{m,j} K_{m,j}. Step 5 then gives μ(A ∖ ⋃_k C_k) = 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: Choose a Borel A′ ⊆ A with A′ = A μ-a.e., so μ(A ∖ A′) = 0.
σ-finiteness of μ⌞A gives Borel S_m covering ℝ^P with μ(A′ ∩ S_m) = μ⌞A(A′ ∩ S_m) < ∞.
The finite Borel measure μ⌞(A′ ∩ S_m) on the σ-compact metric space ℝ^P is regular. This gives compact K_{m,j} ⊆ A′ ∩ S_m with μ((A′ ∩ S_m) ∖ K_{m,j}) < 1/(j+1).
Hence μ((A′ ∩ S_m) ∖ ⋃_j K_{m,j}) = 0. Since A ∖ ⋃_{m,j} K_{m,j} ⊆ (A ∖ A′) ∪ ⋃_m ((A′ ∩ S_m) ∖ ⋃_j K_{m,j}), subadditivity makes it μ-null.
Re-index K_{m,j} by ℕ via Nat.unpair to get compact C_k ⊆ A with μ(A ∖ ⋃_k C_k) = 0.

subproblems.title: Eilenberg finiteness: infinite fibres of a Lipschitz map on a finite-Hᵏ Borel set lie over a Lebesgue-null set
subproblems.statement: Let N, m ∈ ℕ and k := m + 1. Let ℝ^N = Eucl N carry Hᵏ := μHE[k], the normalized Euclidean k-dimensional Hausdorff measure, and let ℝᵏ = Eucl k carry Lebesgue measure Lᵏ (volume). Let E ⊆ ℝ^N be a Borel set with Hᵏ(E) < ∞. Let f : ℝ^N → ℝᵏ be Lipschitz with constant K ∈ [0, ∞), i.e. |f(x) − f(x′)| ≤ K|x − x′| for all x, x′. Then the set {y ∈ ℝᵏ : E ∩ f⁻¹({y}) is infinite} has Lebesgue measure zero.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N m : ℕ) (E : Set (Eucl N)) (f : Eucl N → Eucl (m + 1)) (K : ℝ≥0), MeasurableSet E → (μHE[m + 1] : Measure (Eucl N)) E < ∞ → LipschitzWith K f → (volume : Measure (Eucl (m + 1))) {y : Eucl (m + 1) | (E ∩ f ⁻¹' {y}).Infinite} = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. This is the fibre-counting half of Eilenberg's inequality (Simon, Ch. 2, 1.8(ii); Federer 2.10.25; Lemma 2.3 of Hovila–Järvenpää–Järvenpää–Ledrappier, Geom. Dedicata 161 (2012)), specialised to the finiteness of almost every fibre. It is extracted from step 3(c) of the parent proof, with two changes. Fatou's lemma replaces monotone convergence, so neither the nesting of dyadic cubes nor the identity sup_i N_i = #fibre is needed. Measurable hulls replace σ-compactness of the pieces, so a Borel E suffices.

Notation. k := m + 1 ≥ 1. A point x of ℝ^N = Eucl N has coordinates x_j = x j for j ∈ Fin N; ℝᵏ = Eucl k. Hᵏ := μHE[k] on ℝ^N and Lᵏ := volume on ℝᵏ. Measures are evaluated on arbitrary sets as outer measures, which are monotone and countably subadditive; [0,∞] = ℝ≥0∞. The hypotheses are: E is Borel, Hᵏ(E) < ∞, and f is K-Lipschitz with K ∈ ℝ≥0. Put Y := {y ∈ ℝᵏ : E ∩ f⁻¹({y}) is infinite}. We must show Lᵏ(Y) = 0.

1. Two library facts.
 (a) On ℝᵏ, μHE[k] = Lᵏ. This is Mathlib EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume k; Eucl k is EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k).
 (b) For every S ⊆ ℝ^N, Lᵏ(f(S)) ≤ K^k·Hᵏ(S). Indeed f is K-Lipschitz on S (LipschitzWith.lipschitzOnWith). SimonGMT Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn k then gives μHE[k](f(S)) ≤ (K:[0,∞])^k·μHE[k](S). Finally (a) rewrites the left side as Lᵏ(f(S)).

2. Dyadic cubes. For i ∈ ℕ let g_i : ℝ^N → ℤ^N (ℤ^N := Fin N → ℤ) be g_i(x) := (⌊2^i·x_j⌋)_{j ∈ Fin N}. For z ∈ ℤ^N let Q_i(z) := g_i⁻¹({z}) = {x : z_j ≤ 2^i·x_j < z_j + 1 for every j}.
 (a) For fixed i, the sets Q_i(z) (z ∈ ℤ^N) are pairwise disjoint, being preimages of distinct values of the function g_i. Moreover x ∈ Q_i(g_i(x)) for every x. The index set ℤ^N is countable.
 (b) Each Q_i(z) is Borel. It is the intersection, over the finitely many j, of the preimages of the interval [z_j, z_j + 1) under the continuous maps x ↦ 2^i·x_j. Alternatively, g_i is measurable by Mathlib Int.measurable_floor (module Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Function.Floor), and singletons of ℤ^N are measurable.
 (c) Separation. Let x, x′ ∈ ℝ^N and j ∈ Fin N with 1 ≤ 2^i·|x_j − x′_j|. Then g_i(x) ≠ g_i(x′). Otherwise ⌊2^i x_j⌋ = ⌊2^i x′_j⌋, and Int.abs_sub_lt_one_of_floor_eq_floor gives 2^i|x_j − x′_j| = |2^i x_j − 2^i x′_j| < 1, a contradiction.
 (d) Eventual separation. Let x ≠ x′. A point of ℝ^N is determined by its coordinates (ext), so there is j with c := |x_j − x′_j| > 0. Since 2^i → ∞ and i ↦ 2^i is monotone, there is i₀ with 2^i·c ≥ 1 for all i ≥ i₀. By (c), g_i(x) ≠ g_i(x′) for all i ≥ i₀; that is, ∀ᶠ i in atTop, g_i(x) ≠ g_i(x′).

3. Splitting Hᵏ(E). For every i, Σ_{z∈ℤ^N} Hᵏ(E ∩ Q_i(z)) = Hᵏ(E). The sets E ∩ Q_i(z), z ∈ ℤ^N, are countably many. They are Borel (E is Borel, and 2(b)), pairwise disjoint (2(a)), and their union is E (2(a)). Countable additivity of the measure Hᵏ (Mathlib measure_iUnion) gives the identity.

4. Counting functions and their integrals. Fix i.
 (a) For z ∈ ℤ^N put A_i(z) := f(E ∩ Q_i(z)) ⊆ ℝᵏ and B_i(z) := toMeasurable Lᵏ (A_i(z)). Then B_i(z) is Borel, A_i(z) ⊆ B_i(z), and Lᵏ(B_i(z)) = Lᵏ(A_i(z)) (Mathlib measurableSet_toMeasurable, subset_toMeasurable, measure_toMeasurable).
 (b) Define N_i : ℝᵏ → [0,∞] by N_i(y) := Σ_{z∈ℤ^N} 1_{B_i(z)}(y), the tsum of the indicator functions (B_i z).indicator 1. Each summand is Borel measurable, hence so is N_i, as a countable sum of measurable [0,∞]-valued functions (Measurable.ennreal_tsum, or Measurable.tsum).
 (c) We have ∫ N_i dLᵏ = Σ_z Lᵏ(B_i(z)) = Σ_z Lᵏ(A_i(z)) ≤ Σ_z K^k·Hᵏ(E ∩ Q_i(z)) = K^k·Σ_z Hᵏ(E ∩ Q_i(z)) = K^k·Hᵏ(E). The first equality is the monotone convergence theorem for series (lintegral_tsum) together with ∫ 1_B dLᵏ = Lᵏ(B) for Borel B (lintegral_indicator_one). The second is (a). The inequality is 1(b) with S := E ∩ Q_i(z), applied termwise (ENNReal.tsum_le_tsum). The next equality is ENNReal.tsum_mul_left, and the last is step 3.
 (d) Put C := K^k·Hᵏ(E). Since (K:[0,∞])^k < ∞ and Hᵏ(E) < ∞, C < ∞. By (c), ∫ N_i dLᵏ ≤ C for every i.

5. Large counts on infinite fibres. Let y ∈ Y and M ∈ ℕ. We claim that N_i(y) ≥ M for all sufficiently large i.
 (a) The fibre E ∩ f⁻¹({y}) is infinite, so it contains a finite set T with exactly M elements (Set.Infinite.exists_subset_card_eq).
 (b) For each of the finitely many pairs (x, x′) ∈ T × T, step 2(d) gives ∀ᶠ i, (x ≠ x′ → g_i(x) ≠ g_i(x′)). A finite conjunction of eventually-true statements is eventually true (Filter.eventually_all_finset over T ×ˢ T). Hence there is i₀ such that g_i is injective on T for every i ≥ i₀.
 (c) Fix i ≥ i₀. Every x ∈ T satisfies x ∈ E, f(x) = y and x ∈ Q_i(g_i(x)). Hence y ∈ f(E ∩ Q_i(g_i(x))) = A_i(g_i(x)) ⊆ B_i(g_i(x)), so 1_{B_i(g_i(x))}(y) = 1.
 (d) The image Z := g_i(T) ⊆ ℤ^N is finite with #Z = #T = M (Finset.card_image_of_injOn), and by (c) 1_{B_i(z)}(y) = 1 for every z ∈ Z. All terms of the series N_i(y) are nonnegative, so N_i(y) is at least its finite partial sum over Z (ENNReal.sum_le_tsum): N_i(y) ≥ Σ_{z∈Z} 1_{B_i(z)}(y) = Σ_{z∈Z} 1 = #Z = M.
 (e) Hence, for every y ∈ Y and every M ∈ ℕ, M ≤ N_i(y) for all large i. So M ≤ liminf_{i→∞} N_i(y) (Filter.le_liminf_of_le; the coboundedness side condition is automatic in the complete lattice [0,∞]). M ∈ ℕ is arbitrary and sup_M M = ∞ in [0,∞] (ENNReal.iSup_natCast). Therefore liminf_{i→∞} N_i(y) = ∞ for every y ∈ Y.

6. Fatou's lemma. Let F(y) := liminf_{i→∞} N_i(y). F is Borel measurable (Measurable.liminf). By Fatou's lemma (lintegral_liminf_le) and step 4(d), ∫ F dLᵏ ≤ liminf_{i→∞} ∫ N_i dLᵏ ≤ C < ∞. The second inequality holds because a liminf of a sequence bounded above by C is ≤ C (e.g. Filter.liminf_le_of_frequently_le' with Filter.Frequently.of_forall). A measurable [0,∞]-valued function with finite integral is finite almost everywhere (ae_lt_top). Hence Lᵏ({y : F(y) = ∞}) = 0.

7. Conclusion. By step 5(e), Y ⊆ {y : F(y) = ∞}. By monotonicity of Lᵏ (measure_mono_null), Lᵏ(Y) = 0. That is, volume {y | (E ∩ f ⁻¹' {y}).Infinite} = 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: On ℝᵏ, μHE[k] equals volume. With the SimonGMT Lipschitz image bound this gives Lᵏ(f(S)) ≤ K^k·Hᵏ(S) for every S ⊆ ℝ^N.

The dyadic cubes Q_i(z) = g_i⁻¹{z}, with g_i(x) = (⌊2^i x_j⌋)_j, form a countable Borel partition of ℝ^N at each level i. Two distinct points lie in distinct level-i cubes for all large i, by the floor estimate |a − b| < 1 when ⌊a⌋ = ⌊b⌋.
Countable additivity gives Σ_z Hᵏ(E ∩ Q_i(z)) = Hᵏ(E).
Take Borel hulls B_i(z) ⊇ f(E ∩ Q_i(z)) of equal Lebesgue measure. Then N_i := Σ_z 1_{B_i(z)} is measurable and ∫N_i dLᵏ ≤ K^k·Hᵏ(E) =: C < ∞.
If the fibre over y is infinite, then for every M, N_i(y) ≥ M for all large i, because M fibre points eventually occupy M distinct cubes. Hence liminf_i N_i(y) = ∞.
Fatou gives ∫ liminf_i N_i dLᵏ ≤ C < ∞, so liminf_i N_i < ∞ almost everywhere. Hence the infinite-fibre set is Lᵏ-null.
